$comment: Q78.2/Q78.3/Q79: every framework behind the library, in one place. `points` are for people: short, plain and high level, no rule ids or token names (Q79); the full framework is the Slate doc at `doc.path` (`page.md#anchor`; the library links it through site-links, Q80). `agent` is for agents: rules, a decision procedure (`decide`), the checks to run and the token categories it governs. `appliesTo` says where the library shows it and which component families it governs: page ids, families (`@family`) and sections. The library's Principles block reads this file; npm run agent:index writes it into agent/index.json, each agent/components/{Name}.json and guide/7-principles.md. Edit it here, never in a page or the guide.

frameworks.title: How the library works
points: Every look comes from tokens: change a token and everything that reads it follows.
Parts are sealed. You change them through their options, never by restyling them.
Screens are drawn from data, so content and design stay apart.
Each tier builds on the one below: tokens, fundamentals, compounds, layouts and templates.

rules: Look comes only from tokens; a view, page or content file never carries a class name, style prop, CSS file or raw value.
Components are sealed (no className or style props). Change them by the seam ladder: prop or variant, slot, context attribute, theme, custom part inside a template, then a reviewed core change.
Screens are data: a template manifest names layouts and regions; content JSON fills them; the renderer maps content to layouts, compounds and fundamentals.
Tiers depend downward only: tokens <- fundamentals <- compounds <- layouts <- templates. A fundamental never imports a compound.
Never edit a generated file (tokens.colour.json, tokens.space-shape.json, css/tokens.css, tokens/generated/*, agent/*, generated content schemas).
decide: Search packages/core/agent/index.json for an existing component, block type, layout or template before writing anything.
Pick the lowest tier that meets the need: a fundamental if it is universal, a compound if it arranges fundamentals for one need, a layout for named regions of a screen.
If nothing fits, take the first seam on the ladder that works; a custom part lives in your template as {template}.{Part}.

frameworks.title: The owner’s design rules
points: No stripe on one side to make something stand out.
On or off settings are switches, never buttons.
Segments inside a bar stay square; only the bar’s ends may round.
Space sits at the right level, scrolling reaches the edges, and focus is never cut off.
One version of each thing; most notifications go away on their own.

rules: Never a one-sided accent border (border-left stripe) on a card, button, callout or nav item; use a fill, tint, full outline, icon or badge.
A binary setting is a Switch, never a Button used as an on/off toggle.
Inner segments of a stacked or segmented bar are square; only the outer ends of the whole bar may round.

Pad once at the right interior level (one or two levels below the visual wrapper), never all around a wrapper or per leaf; scroll regions bleed to the surface edge with the scrollbar at the edge; never clip a focus ring.

Every scroll region is a ScrollArea: never `overflow: auto` or `scroll` on any other element, in CSS or inline, since that draws the browser's bar beside the content. Put ScrollArea where the region meets its surface's edge, with its padding on the content inside (its `inset`, or a padded child). A TextArea scrolls its own text and already uses the library's bar.
One component variant per need: no second pattern where one already does the job.
Notifications auto-dismiss; manual dismiss only when the person must read it.
decide: Before adding an accent, choose fill, tint, full outline, icon or badge, in that order of preference.
Before adding a variant, search agent/components/{Name}.json for an existing prop that covers the need.
Before adding padding, find the wrapper that owns the visual edge and pad the first content level inside it; keep the scroll container itself unpadded.

Before letting anything scroll, wrap it in ScrollArea (axis, maxSize, inset; contain only in a popup or modal) placed at its surface's edge; then run the scroll probe (tools/scroll-probe.js) on the screen.

frameworks.title: Presets
points: A preset is a saved set of choices: colour, type, icons, space, shape and surfaces.
One global preset names a choice for each, and every template follows it.
Your own presets sit beside the built-in ones, which can’t be changed.

rules: A preset is a saved choice per category: colour, type, icons, space, shape, material. A global preset names one per category.
Built-in presets are read-only; user presets are saved beside them (design-library.presets) and sync across tabs.
Templates inherit the global preset; a template never hard-codes a category choice.
Choose at run time with @design-library/core/presets (applyGlobalPreset, applyCategoryPreset); change defaults at build time through the token config files.
decide: The product owns this repository look: change the theme (config file, npm run tokens).
The app needs another built-in option: apply a category or global preset at run time.
A person wants to keep their choice: saveCategoryPreset or saveGlobalPreset.

frameworks.title: Colour
points: Parts ask for a colour by its job, such as text or a raised surface, never by its value.
Status colours mean status only, and always come with an icon or words.
Every text and control colour stays readable in light, dark and more contrast.
Decorative colours are for charts and identity, never for meaning.

rules: Components read semantic roles only (color.text, color.bg-raised, color.border-control, state.*); never p.* primitives.
Status meaning only through color.status.{info,success,warning,danger,neutral}.{fg,bg,border,fill,on-fill}, always with an icon or words: never colour alone.
spectrum.* and set.* only for the purpose in their $extensions["org.design-library"].purpose (charts, identity), never for function.
Change colour in packages/core/tokens/colour.config.json, then npm run tokens; never edit tokens.colour.json.
Contrast: text 4.5:1 and non-text 3:1 in light, dark and both contrast levels; tokens:check refuses a theme that misses one.
decide: Is it text, a surface, a line or a control fill? Use the matching color.text*, color.bg*, color.border* or color.bg-control role.
Does it mean a status? Use color.status.* and add an icon or words.
Is it the brand action, link, focus or selection? It already reads the accent; don’t add another.
Is it a category in a chart or an identity? Use a declared set.* or spectrum.* with its purpose.
None fits: add a role through the colour config, never a literal.

frameworks.title: Spacing
points: Everything sits on one small base unit.
Things that belong together sit closer than the groups around them.
The container owns the space between its children, not each child.
Nothing shifts when you hover, focus or wait.
A piece is set apart on its own only when that helps it; a page people use starts with what they came for.

rules: Hierarchy first: before choosing any space, write the page as a tree of groups (every element in exactly one group; members more related to one another than to anything outside). The page is the whole thing; its top-level groups come out of that analysis: header, page content (everything apart from the header and footer) and footer. Then give each group one gap by its depth, and frame only units that gain from being read alone.

Spacing and framing are one model: a frame is one unit in its parent group, placed at the parent's gap and measured from its outer edge; inside it, apply the method again (its content is a tree of its own, with its own gaps). The room between a frame's edge and its content is presentation, not a gap between groups, so it never breaks the inner-smaller-than-outer rule.
One 4 px base unit; components read roles (space.stack-pair, stack-item, stack-group, stack-section, inline-*, inset-*, gutter, margin-page), never a scale step.

Space inside a group is never larger than the space around it, at every node of the tree, the page's top level included: the page content sits from the header and the footer at least as far as its own units sit from one another (a frame is one unit, measured from its outer edge). SiteLayout builds that with its column's padding-block; a layout of your own gets it from the same tree, not from a page-specific rule.
One wrapper per group of the tree (a layout or a compound's part), owning only its children's gap: never one gap serving two levels.
The parent owns space: gap and padding on the container (Stack, Cluster, Grid gap props); never margins set by a sibling position.
Geometry never moves on hover, focus or loading: borders are always there, transparent at rest.
Targets are at least size.target (44 px), or size.target-dense in dense contexts.

Framing (Frame, a hero's `standalone`) isolates a piece and so interrupts reading: frame only what gains from being read alone (a brand opening, a statement, a quote, a call to action, a status message). Task and reference pages (tickets, schedules, lists, forms, settings, detail pages) never frame their heading away from their content: the title and intro sit with the task, which starts in the first view.
decide: Which level? Read it from the tree: the depth of the group whose children the space separates. Pairs (label and value): stack-pair. Items in a list: stack-item. Groups: stack-group. Sections: stack-section. The page content's units, and the page content from the header and footer: stack-page.
Side by side: inline-pair, inline-item, inline-group by the same levels.
Inside a surface: inset-* at the first content level, not on the wrapper.
Need a whole product denser or looser? Change the space option (compact, normal, loose, extra-loose), never single values.

About to frame something? Ask in order: what does the reader gain from seeing it alone? What did they come to this page to do? Would the frame push that below the first view? Nothing gained, or the task delayed: don't frame it. Gained: a stage for an opening (distraction-free when it's the page's only content, peek otherwise), a feature for a piece within the page.

frameworks.title: Visual noise
points: Every line, fill, shadow and icon must tell you something nothing else does.
Use the quietest cue that works: space first, then type, tone, a border, a shadow last.
One box around a group at most; no boxes inside boxes.
Extra cues appear only while they’re needed, such as during a drag.

rules: Every mark (border, divider, fill, shadow, icon, colour, line of text) must carry information nothing else carries.
Cue order, cheapest first: space, alignment, type, tone, border, shadow. One cue per meaning.
Type is a cue: hierarchy comes from the type roles (type.*), not from extra colour, boxes or icons.
At most one enclosure per boundary; no box inside a box.
Transient affordances (drag handles, hover actions, customise cues) appear only while their state is active.
Approved components are never restyled as a side effect of another change.
decide: Can space or alignment group it? Stop there.
Else, can type weight or size? Then tone (a fill step). Then a full hairline. A shadow only if it floats.
Already inside an enclosure? Do not add another; separate with space.

frameworks.title: Elevation and layering
points: Most things sit on the page. Lift something only when it really is above it.
Show height with tone first, a shadow only for what floats, an outline only where tone isn’t enough.
What blocks the page dims it; what doesn’t, leaves it visible.
Things go on top by where they live, never by a bigger number.

rules: Six levels: -1 sunken, 0 canvas, 1 raised, 2 chrome, 3 floating, 4 modal (packages/core/principles/elevation.json).
Tone first, shadow second, edge last. shadow.raised for anchored floating surfaces; shadow.overlay for free floating and modal. No shadow at rest on content or chrome.
z-index only as var(--layer-*) or a c.<part>.layer token aliasing one; never a number, never an inline zIndex.
Popups open in the top layer (popover attribute); dialogs as modal dialog elements; the layer token is only the fallback order.
A component ordering its own parts with layer.behind or layer.raised sets isolation: isolate on the holder.
decide: Pick the level from the ladder by what the surface does, then the layer by the "Choosing a layer" questions (elevation.json, printed below in the guide); the first yes decides.
Hidden behind something? Find the ancestor that starts a stacking context and move the thing to the top layer; never raise the number.

frameworks.title: Materials
points: Each surface is made of a material that says what layer it belongs to.
Content surfaces are always solid; only bars and floating surfaces may be frosted.
Frosted is one switch for the whole product, and goes solid wherever reading could suffer.
Never frosted on frosted.

rules: A component names its material (canvas, sunken, raised, tint, control, chrome, floating, modal, scrim, veil); tokens decide how it is painted.
The content layer (canvas, sunken, raised, tint, control) is always solid; only chrome and floating may be frosted.
Frosted is one global setting (data-material="frosted" or "solid" on the root); never per component.
Never glass on glass: a floating surface inside another is solid.
Reduced transparency, more contrast, forced colours and print are solid. Blur radius never animates.
Chrome, floating and modal surfaces carry data-material and data-elevation (the add-on seam).
decide: A page or region: canvas; rails and wells: sunken; a card or field: raised or control fill; the current item: tint.
A bar content scrolls under: chrome. A popup or free toolbar: floating. A blocking surface: modal over the scrim. Controls over media: veil.

frameworks.title: Motion
points: Motion shows how things move from one state to the next; it never decorates.
What stays across a change morphs instead of vanishing and coming back.
Most changes take a fifth of a second; nothing jumps.
What you drive directly, like typing or dragging, answers instantly.
With reduced motion, travel stops and gentle fades stay.

rules: Components read motion roles (duration.quick, change, move, move-far, shared; easing.standard, enter, exit, linear), never the private scale (fast, medium, slow).
Every visual value change (fill, border colour, shadow, opacity) eases at duration.change (200 ms); nothing jumps.
Content present in both states morphs (same wrapper, shared element) instead of disappearing and reappearing.
Zero latency where a person drives a value (typing, arrow-key steps, drags, sliders): no transition on that value (packages/core/motion/zero-latency.json).
With reduced motion travel snaps and fades stay; never transition: all; never a literal duration or curve.
decide: Does the person drive the value directly? No transition on it.
Is it a colour, fill, border, shadow or opacity change? duration.change with easing.standard.
Does something travel or resize? duration.move or move-far; arriving uses easing.enter, leaving easing.exit.
Is the same thing on both sides of a view change? A shared-element morph (duration.shared).

frameworks.title: States
points: Every change you make is confirmed where you made it.
Loading, saving, success, error and empty each have one place and one look.
An error keeps what you typed and always offers a way to recover.
An empty list says why it’s empty and what to do next.

rules: Every committed change is confirmed where it was made for at least duration.confirm-min.
Each state has one owner level (app, view, section, component, field) and one look: loading, saving, success, error, empty.
Views and sections load with shimmer skeletons; one bottom notification pill, one line, at most three.
Errors keep the input and always offer a recovery (Retry, Revert).
Empty states live in the content’s own wrapper and say why and what to do.
decide: Field-level change: the field shows pending, confirmed or failed (useCommit).
Whole view loading: a skeleton in the view, keeping the old view until the new one is ready.
A result of an action elsewhere: one notification pill that auto-dismisses.
Nothing to show: EmptyState inside the list or region, with the next action.

frameworks.title: Waiting
points: Never a silent wait: say what’s happening, honestly.
Keep what’s on screen until the new view is ready.
Never block or lose what someone is typing while something loads.

rules: Classify the wait: instant, responsive, waiting or long, and give the matching feedback.
Never block or lose input during a wait; keep the old view until the new one is ready.
One honest status; never a silent wait.
Indicators wait duration.indicator-delay before showing and stay at least duration.indicator-min.
decide: Under about 100 ms: no indicator. Up to about a second: a local indicator after the delay. Longer: progress with words. Very long: progress plus a way to keep working.

frameworks.title: Words
points: Plain words a person would say, as few as do the job.
Buttons say what they do; errors say what happened and how to fix it.
The same thing is always called by the same name.

rules: Words come from content or props, never hard-coded in a component.
Sentence case, plain words, curly apostrophes; buttons are verbs that say the result.
Errors say what happened and how to fix it; never blame the person.
One name per thing across the product (the glossary).
Every icon-only control has an accessible name, shown by Tooltip.
decide: Label: the noun or the verb, two to four words.
Error: what happened, then the fix, in one or two short sentences.
Empty state: why it is empty, then the action.

frameworks.title: Showing information
points: Show it rather than tell it when a picture is faster to understand.
Choose the form that lets someone understand and act with the least reading.
Show it exactly as it is when accuracy or the exact words matter.
Every picture, icon and chart has a text alternative.

rules: Run the reasoning chain in docs/visual-representation.md before choosing text, an icon, a picture, an illustration, media or a chart.
Show as is when accuracy, verbatim words or the content itself must be preserved.
Every visual carries a text alternative; charts never mislead (zero baselines for bars, honest scales).
Chart categories read set.* or spectrum.* with their declared purpose; status never by colour alone.
Inner bar segments stay square.
decide: Follow the agent procedure in docs/visual-representation.md (The chain as an agent procedure) and its Agent checklist.
